title: Garlic and Parsley Butter Pull-Apart Rolls
changes_from_base: Plain-flour dough baked in a rectangular dish, egg-washed, then soaked in garlic and parsley butter.
summary: Soft, golden pull-apart rolls drenched straight from the oven in melted garlic and parsley butter.
equipment: large bowl or stand mixer with dough hook
cling film or a clean tea towel

ingredients.note: beaten with a pinch of salt

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Whisk the milk, cooled melted butter and 1 egg in a large bowl, then tip in the flour and yeast and mix to a shaggy dough with no dry patches. Cover and rest 15 min so the flour hydrates.

steps.title: Knead
steps.text: Add the sugar and salt and knead 8-10 min by machine on medium (or 12 min by hand), until the dough is smooth, stretchy and only slightly tacky.

steps.title: Rise
steps.text: Shape into a ball, return to a lightly greased bowl, cover and leave about 1 h, until doubled.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Butter the dish. Cut the dough into 12 pieces of roughly 50 g, curl your palm over each one and roll it on an unfloured worktop into a taut ball. Set them in the dish in three rows of four, cover and leave 30-40 min, until the balls press against each other.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Heat the oven to 180 °C (160 °C fan). Brush the tops with the salted beaten egg and bake about 20 min, until deep golden; the centre roll reads 88-90 °C.

steps.title: Garlic butter
steps.text: While the rolls bake, melt the butter with the garlic over low heat for 2 min without letting it colour, then stir in the parsley and the pinch of salt. Spoon it over the hot rolls straight from the oven, let them soak for 5 min and serve warm.

tips: Grate the garlic finely so it melts into the butter instead of sitting in lumps.
Keep the butter on a low heat; browned garlic tastes harsh.
Pour the butter over the rolls the moment they leave the oven so it soaks in.
storage: Keep cooled rolls in an airtight bag at room temperature for up to 2 days. Rewarm at 180 °C for 5 min; freeze for up to 1 month. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
